(a) The emission and absorption of electromagnetic radiation by a Josephson junction driven by a dc bias current is a process of photon-assisted macro-scopic quantum tunneling (PAMQTT) in which the tunneling current is enhanced or suppressed by the presence of a quantized electromagnetic field.

(i) the energy spectrum of the JPW quanta is strongly dependent on the junction length, (ii) the emission/absorption amplitudes are proportional to the length of the junction, (iii) the emission/ absorption spectra show sharp resonances at the frequencies of the JPW eigenmodes, (iv) these resonances can be used to tune the emission/absorbtion amplitudes by the applied dc current, (v) the emission/ absortion spectra show

the interaction between a long Josephson Junction and an electromagnetic field is strongly enhanced when the junction length is comparable to the radiation wavelength and that photon-assisted macroscopical quantum tunnelling shows resonances when the radiation frequency coincides with the eigenfrequencies of current-driven Josephson plasma waves.
